The Administration Partner plays a central role in an innovative service model designed to maximise front line support across a group of Villages.

Reporting to the Operations Business Manager, this role provides high-quality, remote administrative support that enables Village-based teams to focus more of their time on providing exceptional customer service and resident experiences.

  • Use your operational expertise and experience to improve how front line teams deliver exceptional customer service
  • Provide administration support to Village and Care teams, keeping communication clear and ensuring information, enquiries, and requests are actioned in a timely manner.

  • Financial Administration, create and maintain purchase orders within delegated authority.
  • Be the first point of contact for AP for investigating and resolving billing issues. 
  • Building strong working relationships across a diverse range of stakeholders and teams.

Qualifications:

You’re an organised, proactive administrator with strong communication skills who enjoys bringing structure and clarity to busy environments. You’re comfortable juggling multiple priorities, working autonomously, and supporting stakeholders with confidence and professionalism.

You take pride in producing high‑quality outputs, communicating clearly, and finding smarter ways of working that help teams perform at their best.

  • Previous administration experience in the aged care and retirement living preferred. 
  • Proven ability to deliver great internal and external customer service, build positive relationships with village teams, and show genuine care for residents and their experience, including when interacting remotely.
  • Experience in managing accounts payable and receivable. 
  • Skilled in data entry and in keeping databases accurate and up to date.  
  • Strong computer literacy, especially in Microsoft Excel, Copilot, Word, Teams, Outlook and PowerPoint. 
  • Comfortable suggesting improvements to standardised processes to help save time and use resources more efficiently. 
  • Able to handle confidential information with discretion and integrity. 
  • Highly organised and able to pick up and effectively manage multiple tasks at short notice. 
  • Ability to learn and adapt to existing and new software systems, including AI assistance tools 
  • Be honest, punctual and reliable.

job.description:

Job Description:

This is a senior operational leadership role with real influence. You’ll work closely with the Chief Operations Officer – NZ, Operations SLT, GM Village Operations, Group Operations Managers and village leaders to strengthen the way health, safety and wellbeing is understood, led and managed in day-to-day operations. 

The role is not about HSW doing the work for Operations. It is about enabling operational leaders to own HSW outcomes, use reliable information, make informed risk decisions and demonstrate effective control of health, safety and wellbeing performance without constant HSW intervention. 

What you’ll be doing 

In this role, you’ll lead the Operations HSW approach by: 

  • Leading and sustaining the HSW relationship with the Chief Operations Officer – NZ, Operations SLT, GM Village Operations, Group Operations Managers and key operational support leaders 

  • Embedding HSW into operational planning, performance discussions, delivery rhythms and decision-making 

  • Owning Operations HSW system performance, including agreed headline measures, reporting quality, investigation closure, corrective-action closure and risk-review completion 

  • Leading the operation-specific implementation of Summerset’s Critical Risk programme and ensuring critical controls are understood, planned into work and verified in practice 

  • Partnering with Property, Facilities and Operations leaders to support practical, risk-based contractor management in resident-facing environments 

  • Leading Operations injury management, including TPA oversight, return-to-work discipline, complex claim escalation and ACC AEP audit readiness 

  • Championing effective use of Donesafe across incident management, risk reviews, audits, contractor management, injury management evidence and corrective-action tracking 

  • Leading, coaching and supporting HSW Advisors – Operations, including a risk-based advisor coverage model aligned to operational priorities 

  • Using data, reporting and operational insight to make risk, performance trends, dependencies and trade-offs visible to senior leaders and governance forums 

  • Supporting wellbeing and Culture of Care initiatives, including psychosocial risk, injury prevention, recovery support and leader capability 

Qualifications:

About you 

You’ll be an experienced HSW leader who can operate with both strategic influence and practical discipline. You’ll understand how to shift leaders from HSW dependency to HSW ownership, while keeping systems, assurance and performance visible and well managed. 

You’ll bring: 

  • Senior health, safety and wellbeing experience in complex operations, aged care, healthcare, property, facilities or another multi-site environment 

  • Strong knowledge of New Zealand health and safety legislation, ACC Accredited Employer Programme requirements and practical application in operational settings 

  • Demonstrated experience in injury management, return-to-work oversight, TPA relationships and claims governance 

  • Strong assurance, audit, incident investigation, critical risk management and corrective-action effectiveness capability 

  • Confidence influencing senior operational leaders and supporting informed decisions about risk, performance and trade-offs 

  • Proven ability to use data, reporting and operational insight to identify trends, communicate risk and drive practical improvement 

  • Strong people leadership and coaching capability, including developing advisors and managing workload across a distributed team 

  • A calm, credible and pragmatic style, with the confidence to challenge, simplify and improve how work is done 

You’ll be someone who can work through complexity, build trust with senior and site-based leaders, and keep the focus on what matters most: effective controls, better decisions, stronger ownership and safe outcomes for our people, residents, contractors and visitors.

Additional Information:

Why join us? 

At Summerset, health, safety and wellbeing is about more than process and compliance. It is about leadership, ownership and creating environments where our people can do their best work and our residents feel safe, supported and at home. 

This is a visible Group role with the opportunity to influence senior operational leaders, strengthen HSW system performance and lead meaningful improvement across our New Zealand village operations.

Reporting to the Head of P&C Shared Services and working closely with the Chief People Officer, you will be the trusted subject matter expert for remuneration, incentives, benefits and reward governance. This role will suit someone who genuinely enjoys complexity and is energised by evolving remuneration landscapes, including IEAs, CEAs, unions, collective bargaining, Australian Modern Awards, STI, LTI and remuneration package design.

What you’ll be doing

  • Own and evolve Summerset’s remuneration and reward framework across New Zealand and Australia.
  • Lead annual remuneration review activity, including planning, analysis, recommendations, governance papers and leader guidance.
  • Provide expert advice on complex remuneration matters, including IEA and CEA environments, union considerations, collective bargaining impacts and internal equity.
  • Support Australian remuneration design and compliance, with a particular focus on Modern Awards and remuneration package structures.
  • Manage and enhance STI, LTI, benefits, recognition and reward programmes so they are competitive, practical and aligned to business priorities.
  • Use market data, benchmarking and internal insights to support evidence-based decision making for executives, leaders and the Board.
  • Partner closely with P&C, Finance, Legal, Payroll and senior leaders to ensure reward practices are well understood, well governed and well executed.
  • Work with a reporting analyst with remuneration experience, along with shared service coordinators who provide support during remuneration review and peak activity periods.

This is not a “keep the lights on” reward role. You will be joining a business that is growing, maturing and continuing to build more sophisticated reward practices across two countries. There are no direct reports, but you will not be doing it alone. You will have analytical and shared services support, strong executive connection and the opportunity to shape how reward supports our people and our business.

Qualifications:

To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:

  • Solid remuneration and reward experience in a complex organisation.
  • Strong NZ and Australian remuneration knowledge, including practical experience with Australian Modern Awards and remuneration package structures.
  • Confidence advising on complex employment environments, including IEAs, CEAs, unions and collective bargaining considerations.
  • Experience designing, reviewing or governing salary structures, benefits, STI, LTI, bonus schemes and recognition programmes.
  • Strong analytical capability, with the ability to turn remuneration data, market insights and benchmarking into clear recommendations.
  • The credibility to influence senior leaders and translate complex reward concepts into practical, commercially grounded advice.
  • Excellent judgement, attention to detail and a strong understanding of governance, confidentiality and risk.
  • A continuous improvement mindset and the confidence to work in an environment that is growing, changing and becoming more sophisticated.

Additional Information:

This is a great opportunity for a reward specialist who wants to be close to decision making, close to the CPO and close to the work that really matters. You will have room to influence, improve and build reward practices that support a growing workforce across New Zealand and Australia.
